findings.paper_title: Treasury Management Outturn Report 2025-26 for Council
findings.headline: Council exceeded its interest rate exposure prudential indicator, holding higher variable-rate investments than approved
findings.detail: The council maintained average variable-rate investments of £18.722 million during 2025/26, exceeding the £15 million anticipated level in its prudential indicators. This increased the council's sensitivity to a 1% interest rate movement to £187,000 compared to the expected £150,000. The council acknowledges this exceedance in its key messages, noting it produced no adverse financial impact because actual interest rate movements were smaller than anticipated.
findings.matters: Exceeding formal prudential indicators shows the council's risk management framework was not followed, raising questions about control procedures and forecast accuracy—both relevant to credit risk assessment
findings.figures: £18.722m average variable-rate investments vs £15m anticipated; 1% interest rate sensitivity £187k vs £150k expected
findings.quote: The interest rate exposure indicator was exceeded, albeit it did not result in any negative implications for the Council, as explained within the report.

findings.paper_title: Capital Programme Report to Council - July 2026
findings.headline: Five-year programme assumes continued Welsh Government grant funding, but future allocations are uncertain and could be lower
findings.detail: The council's ability to keep external borrowing low and maintain the capital programme depends on unhypothecated grant funding from Welsh Government. The council explicitly notes that these annual allocations are determined by the Welsh Government budget process and there is a risk that future allocations could be lower than current levels, which would either reduce programme scope or force increased borrowing.
findings.matters: A lender would be concerned about external funding dependency that is outside the council's control, and whether lower grants would force unwanted borrowing or programme compression
findings.figures: £1.506m grant received 2025/26; total unallocated across 2027/28–2030/31 is 'just over £13 million'
findings.quote: the amount of unhypothecated funding (supported borrowing and General Capital Grant) for future years has been modelled in line with existing allocations. In reality, the annual allocations are determined as part of the Welsh Government budget setting process and, therefore, there is a risk that future allocations could be lower than the current year.

findings.paper_title: Capital Programme Report to Council - July 2026
findings.headline: Contingency falls to £240,000 on a £40.6m annual programme—just 0.6% coverage—after spending the Welsh Government grant
findings.detail: The council is committing the full £1.506m grant received in 2025/26 to capital schemes, reducing 2026/27 unallocated resources from £1.746m to £240k. The council describes this as 'adequate' for cost overruns or new pressures, but any material scheme slippage or price increase would exhaust contingency and force contingency to be brought forward from future years.
findings.matters: A lender would assess whether this level of contingency is sufficient to absorb the cost volatility typical in capital programmes, and whether the council can manage risk if multiple schemes overrun in the same year
findings.figures: £240k unallocated against £40.612m total 2026/27 programme; £1.506m committed to new schemes
findings.quote: In committing this resource to the priorities outlined earlier in the report, it will reduce the uncommitted allocation in 2026/27 to £240,000. This is felt to be an adequate level of resource in order to mitigate against the risk of cost increases against existing schemes or new pressures emerging during the remainder of the year.

findings.paper_title: Council Report - 2025_26 Governance and Audit Cttee Annual report
findings.headline: 2024/25 external audit of Statement of Accounts remains incomplete due to unspecified issues
findings.detail: The Committee has not yet received the ISA 260 audit report on the 2024/25 Statement of Accounts. The paper states this is 'due to issues identified which are being dealt with'. Almost a year after the financial year end, the external audit remains incomplete. The paper indicates resolution will occur 'during the current financial year' (2025/26), but no timeline or detail on the issues is provided.
findings.matters: Delayed external audit sign-offs with unspecified problems are a material concern for lenders. They suggest either issues with the council's financial systems, the accounts themselves, or both. Until the audit concludes, the 2024/25 financial position is not independently verified.
findings.figures: 2024/25 audit outstanding as of July 2026; planned resolution during 2025/26 financial year
findings.quote: The Committee has not yet received detailed reports on the 2024/25 Statement of Accounts including the ISA 260 (a report issued to those charged with Governance) for consideration due to issues identified which are being dealt with.

findings.paper_title: Head of Internal Audit Annual Report 2025_26 - July 2026 Governance Audit Committee
findings.headline: Community Hall Governance and Third Sector major grants audits show limited control effectiveness with less than 50% of expected controls operating.
findings.detail: Two audits received 'limited' opinions, indicating less than half of expected controls are operating as intended. These covered Community Hall Governance and Third Sector major grants. Follow-up audits are scheduled for 2026/27 to assess progress.
findings.matters: Limited control effectiveness in resource governance areas means the council may not be adequately monitoring allocation and use of community resources and grant funds.
findings.figures: Two audits with limited opinions; threshold is less than 50% of expected controls operating as intended
findings.quote: There were two audits in the year with a limited audit opinions i.e. less than fifty percent of the expected controls operating as intended by management. These related to Community Hall Governance and Third Sector major grants.

findings.paper_title: Head of Internal Audit Annual Report 2025_26 - July 2026 Governance Audit Committee
findings.headline: Elective home education service has two high priority control failures in assessing applications and conducting annual case reviews.
findings.detail: Applications are not being assessed within the eight-week guideline, and not all cases are being reviewed annually. These are statutory requirements for home education oversight. An action plan is in place with follow-up audit scheduled for 2026/27.
findings.matters: Failure to meet statutory timelines and conduct required reviews indicates regulatory non-compliance and potential capacity constraints, creating legal and reputational risk.
findings.quote: Both related to the Elective home education service which were previously reported to the Committee. The issues were that not all applications are assessed within the eight-week guideline and not all cases are reviewed annually.

findings.headline: Children's Services transition achieved without using most of allocated contingency, but this was exceptional performance unlikely to repeat
findings.detail: Children's Services was allocated a £1.986m transition fund to manage change and cost reduction. Only £53k was drawn, leaving £1.93m underspent. The report attributes this to 'the speed of change' in implementing a new operating model, reduction in placement numbers (438 budgeted, 427 actual), and vacancy savings. This one-off improvement underpinned the overall positive outturn.
findings.matters: While this year's improvement is positive, a lender should note it relied on exceptional pace of transformation and may not repeat; Children's Services remains a major cost base (£125.7m budget, nearly 51% of net budget).
findings.figures: £1.986m transition fund; only £53k used; placement numbers 427 vs 438 budgeted
findings.quote: However, the speed of change has been significant and meant that almost none of the transition budget was required. This resulted in a significant underspend against the Centrally Held Budgets line, which has underpinned the overall position.

findings.headline: Structural cost pressure on temporary homelessness accommodation where DWP subsidy does not cover full costs
findings.detail: The council recorded a £471k adverse variance against Housing Benefit Subsidy, with the report identifying this as a permanent feature: 'Housing Benefit costs that aren't eligible for HB Subsidy from the Department of Work & Pensions (DWP)' arise 'in relation to high-cost temporary accommodation for homeless individuals, where the DWP subsidy rate is fixed and doesn't cover the full cost incurred.' This is not a one-off or correctable issue.
findings.matters: This represents an unmatched cost exposure where statutory duties (housing homeless) generate costs that are not subsidised by central government at the rate incurred; it creates structural budget risk that cannot be externally resolved.
findings.figures: £471k adverse variance; described as ongoing scenario
findings.quote: Housing Benefit (HB) costs that aren't eligible for HB Subsidy from the Department of Work & Pensions (DWP). This scenario arises in relation to high-cost temporary accommodation for homeless individuals, where the DWP subsidy rate is fixed and doesn't cover the full cost incurred.

findings.headline: Capital programme experiencing persistent slippage, with £3.668m carried forward and limited contingency for cost overruns
findings.detail: Beyond planned slippage, the council identified £3.668m of unplanned slippage at year-end across projects including asset management (£739k), 3G pitches (£451k combined), and professional fees (£1.2m). The report explicitly warns that 'overall unallocated capital resources remain relatively low' and project managers must mitigate cost increases 'from within allocated budgets, or by seeking external funding, as much as possible.'
findings.matters: Persistent capital slippage and thin contingency indicate delivery risk on infrastructure investment and may signal planning or execution challenges that could delay service improvements or asset replacement.
findings.figures: £3.668m unplanned slippage; overall contingency described as 'relatively low'
findings.quote: overall unallocated capital resources remain relatively low and, as a result, project managers will need to mitigate cost increases that emerge from within allocated budgets, or by seeking external funding, as much as possible.

findings.headline: Recycling and Waste services under pressure: £302k adverse variance from agency staffing and reduced recyclate income
findings.detail: Neighbourhoods & Environment reporting £90k overall adverse variance, with Waste and Recycling services driven by £302k pressure. Main cost drivers: agency staff costs for collection services, plant repairs, and significantly reduced income from sale of recyclates (commodity market driven). Partly offset by vacancy savings elsewhere in service, but underlying cost base appears to have increased.
findings.matters: Rising waste disposal costs and reliance on volatile recyclate markets create structural cost pressures; high agency staffing suggests permanent staffing shortfall or contract redesign issue.
findings.figures: £302k adverse variance in Waste services; total Neighbourhoods & Environment adverse variance £90k
findings.quote: The main pressure area is in relation to Recycling and Waste services (£302,000) linked to agency staff costs, plant repairs and reduced income from the sale of recyclates

findings.headline: Three schools forecast to close 2025-26 in deficit positions within school reserve envelope
findings.detail: School collective reserves forecast to reach £3.079m (3.71% of total school budget) by end of 2025-26, down from £4.731m previous year. Within this aggregate position, three schools have anticipated closing deficit positions. Council committed to 'close monitoring and support' throughout remainder of year, indicating emergent control and governance challenge in school financial management.
findings.matters: School deficits indicate control weakness in a major spend area and create future calls on council reserves through intervention, support, and potential restructuring costs.
findings.figures: Three schools in deficit; school reserves at 3.71% of budget (£3.079m); £1.65m reduction forecast in school reserves
findings.quote: contained within that overall position are three schools with anticipated closing deficit positions. Close monitoring of, and support to, the schools in deficit, as well as those at risk of entering a deficit position over the medium term, will continue throughout the remainder of the year

findings.headline: General Fund Balance declining significantly: £11.998m (2024) to forecast £9.205m (2026)
findings.detail: General Fund reserves falling by £1.7m year-on-year, with overall reserve reduction of circa £7.8m anticipated in 2025-26. While still above council minimums (£5.8m authorised, £7.5m operational), the consistent downward trajectory is concerning. Combined with school reserves falling to £3.071m and overall council reserves declining from £41.302m to £33.5m forecast, financial cushion is materially reduced.
findings.matters: Declining reserves reduce the council's capacity to absorb unexpected cost pressures, service demand spikes, or income shortfalls, increasing financial vulnerability.
findings.figures: General Fund Balance: £11.998m (March 2024), £10.901m (March 2025 actual), £9.205m (March 2026 forecast); total reserve reduction ~£7.8m; school reserves forecast to £3.079m (3.71% of school budget)

findings.headline: Housing Benefit subsidy gap creating permanent structural overspend with no funded solution
findings.detail: Temporary accommodation costs for homeless individuals continue to exceed DWP subsidy rates, creating £178k adverse variance at Month 7. £158k of the £517k total 'at risk' mitigations relate to Housing Benefit and are described as 'unlikely to materially change'. Council has factored this persistent pressure into 2026-27 budget, indicating expectation it will continue. DWP subsidy rate is fixed and does not cover actual costs incurred.
findings.matters: This is a demand-driven cost pressure with no fundable solution, reducing financial flexibility and exposing the council to unbudgeted costs driven by homelessness demand factors outside its control.
findings.figures: £178k Month 7 adverse variance; £158k at risk on 2025-26 mitigations; £414k estimated overall 2026-27 pressure (target reduction of £100k)
findings.quote: there continues to be an adverse variance as a result of Housing Benefit (HB) costs that aren't eligible for HB Subsidy from the Department of Work & Pensions (DWP), linked to high-cost temporary accommodation where the DWP subsidy rate is fixed and doesn't cover the full cost incurred.

findings.headline: Capital programme slippage of £15.37m expected; only 41% spent despite seven months into year
findings.detail: Council's capital budget working base of £53.87m has £15.37m planned slippage carried forward. Major schemes affected include Pontypool Regeneration LUF (£5.4m), Sustainable Communities for Learning (£3.9m), The British (£3.5m), and Waste Transfer Station (£2.1m). Expenditure to date of only 41% despite scheme budgets typically weighted to second half of year suggests additional unplanned slippage likely by year end. Grant funding approvals will need to be sought for carried-forward schemes.
findings.matters: Capital delivery delays indicate project and scheme management challenges, potentially defer service improvements, and create uncertainty in asset deployment and debt servicing profiles.
findings.figures: £15.37m planned slippage from £53.87m working budget; 41% expenditure to date; major slippages: Pontypool Regeneration £5.4m, Sustainable Communities £3.9m, The British £3.5m, Waste Transfer Station £2.1m
findings.quote: the level of actual expenditure to date is circa 41% of the total budget... the level of spend currently achieved would suggest that additional slippage is likely to be identified by the end of the financial year. This slippage will need to be carried forward into 2026/27, in order to allow schemes to be completed.

findings.paper_title: Capital Strategy 2026_27 Audit Committee xx 2026 Draft (1)
findings.headline: Council pursuing asset rationalization and external grant maximization as primary levers to create capital headroom
findings.detail: With limited headroom for new borrowing, the council plans to 'subject [its] asset base to review, with a focus on optimisation and rationalisation' and notes 'there will continue to be a heavy reliance upon external grant funding.' This indicates capital receipts are insufficient and the council is dependent on factors outside its control (grant awards, asset sale values).
findings.matters: Over-reliance on discretionary government grants and unpredictable asset sales makes the capital programme fragile and exposes the council to cuts in national funding
findings.quote: External funding should be maximised and used to pursue the Council's existing objectives wherever possible, rather than being used to pursue new initiatives at the expense of existing need and challenges.

findings.paper_title: Capital Strategy 2026_27 Audit Committee xx 2026 Draft (1)
findings.headline: Significant unmet demand for capital, particularly school estate condition and Additional Learning Needs, may require revenue sacrifice
findings.detail: The council identifies 'significant issues within the school estate' and 'demand pressures, such as those within Children's Services and the growth in Additional Learning Needs.' It states it 'may not be possible to meet the full demand for capital expenditure' and may need to 'commit revenue resources for the purpose of new borrowing, however that would need to be balanced against other priorities.'
findings.matters: Unmet capital demand in schools and children's services represents a growing unfunded liability; any decision to fund it from revenue would further squeeze service budgets
findings.figures: £57m capital programme over 5 years (2026/27–2030/31) excluding resources to be allocated
findings.quote: It may not be possible to meet the full demand for capital expenditure and resources and, therefore, clear prioritisation of objectives will be key to ensuring the financial sustainability of the Council in the future.

findings.paper_title: Capital Strategy 2026_27 Audit Committee xx 2026 Draft (1)
findings.headline: Revenue budget faces ongoing pressure from high interest rates and debt servicing costs amid reported in-year overspend
findings.detail: The council reports an 'in-year overspend position and the challenge in setting a balanced budget for 2026/27.' Interest costs and MRP (principal repayments) will consume 3.54% of the net revenue stream in 2026/27. The paper states 'interest rates remain high, which reduces the spending power of any revenue funding' and notes the council 'already has a need to externalise existing internal borrowing, which will come at a cost.'
findings.matters: In-year overspend coupled with rising borrowing costs signal structural budget difficulty and limited headroom for further financial pressure
findings.figures: Finance costs 3.54% of net revenue stream (2026/27); 2025/26 revised showed in-year overspend
findings.quote: It is important to recognise the challenging financial situation within which the Council is operating. This is evidenced within the revenue budget, given the recently reported in-year overspend position and the challenge in setting a balanced budget for 2026/27.

findings.paper_title: Capital Strategy 2026_27 Audit Committee xx 2026 Draft (1)
findings.headline: Long-term external borrowing forecast to increase by £8.7m to refinance maturing temporary borrowing
findings.detail: Gross borrowing forecast rises from £128.01m (2025/26) to £136.75m (2026/27). The strategy notes this increase is 'largely due to the need to refinance current temporary borrowing and because of reducing internal borrowing capacity.' This means the council is running down cash reserves and will need to take on new debt at prevailing market rates.
findings.matters: Rising external borrowing increases interest cost exposure and refinancing risk; a lender needs to know the council is moving toward greater reliance on external funding
findings.quote: Long-term external borrowing is expected to increase, largely due to the need to refinance current temporary borrowing and because of reducing internal borrowing capacity.

findings.paper_title: Capital Strategy 2026_27 Audit Committee xx 2026 Draft (1)
findings.headline: Capital programme reduced 30% year-on-year due to low resources and constrained borrowing capacity
findings.detail: The 2026/27 capital programme is £26.8m, down from £38.5m in 2025/26. The council explicitly states it has a 'relatively low level of its own available capital resources, diminishing capacity for internal borrowing, plus a limited ability to afford new external borrowing.' This reduction reflects fundamental resource constraints, not temporary timing.
findings.matters: Reduced capital investment signals financial stress and limits the council's ability to maintain its asset base or invest in service improvements, both of concern to lenders
findings.quote: The size of the programme is smaller than in previous years, which reflects the low level of capital resources available.
